feature: A redline copy pastes as the picture in Chromium
summary: Checked on this Mac, nothing sent anywhere: Shift Command C pastes the redlined picture into a rich box in Chrome and Edge, and the spec list into a plain text box, the same as Safari's engine and TextEdit. No change to the app.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. The local test page is docs/design/references/redline-paste-check/index.html; open it in Chrome.

try.do: Open a screenshot, add two measurements with the Measure tool (press i), and press Shift Command C.
Click the rich box and press Command V. The picture lands, with no text.
Click the plain textarea and press Command V. The spec list lands.
Read the record under the boxes: the page was handed both the text and image.png.
In Slack or Discord, paste into a message box and do not press Return. Note whether it shows the picture as an attachment or the list as text, then clear the box.

evaluate: When you paste into a Slack or Discord message box (without sending), do you get the picture?
If a chat ever pastes the list instead, would you rather Shift Command C carry the picture alone, with the list on its own command?
Is a picture-only paste into a rich box what you expect from a redline hand-off?
rough: Slack, Discord and Teams were not tried: each decides with its own paste code, and the loop never pastes into a real chat. Chromium hands them both the picture and the list, so the last step above is the one check left, and it is yours.

Chromium lists the text before the picture in what it hands a page (WebKit lists the picture first). A chat that takes the first thing it finds would pick the list there; nothing seen so far does that.

TextEdit itself was not driven: the loop has no permission to control other apps. A rich text view set up the way TextEdit's rich document is took the picture; a plain one took the list. No mock covers this surface.
